research-development.tsx.marineAbstract: Using effective records on Chinese marine intangible cultural heritage from CNKI, Wanfang and VIP for 2003–2022, this study uses CiteSpace to analyse and visualise authors, institutions, keywords and their evolution. The findings are threefold. First, publication volume rose sharply in 2017 following the emphasis on strengthening China’s maritime strategy at the 19th National Congress; although research output increased over the two-decade period, its overall scale remained limited. Second, research hotspots mainly concern the development of individual marine-heritage cases and approaches to heritage preservation and transmission. Third, emerging research frontiers include supporting rural revitalisation through marine intangible cultural heritage and promoting sustainable development through living transmission, digital technologies and other innovative approaches. Future research can be broadened and deepened through interdisciplinary work, learning from international experience, stronger collaboration and exchange, and focused case studies.
research-development.tsx.fishersAbstract: The symbiotic relationship between enhancing fishermen’s livelihood resilience and the sustainable development of fisheries is increasingly significant. In recent times, the frequent occurrence of climate-related and natural disasters poses substantial risks to the livelihoods of fishermen in Guangdong Province. This context underscores the urgency of analysing factors that influence the resilience of fishermen’s livelihoods, which is crucial for disaster resistance and resilience enhancement. Utilising a three-dimensional livelihood resilience framework, this paper explores the endogenous relationships and resilience trends among various factors within the livelihood resilience system of fishermen in Guangdong Province. Additionally, it forecasts and simulates the resilience shifts of exogenous variables across multiple scenarios under the policy of ‘Remote Utilization and Ecological Development’. Our findings indicate that the key components bolstering the livelihood resilience of Guangdong’s fishermen include their capacity for learning, buffering, and self-organisation. Each system incorporates a ‘disaster prevention – disaster reduction – disaster relief’ cycle to combat disastrous impacts effectively. Moreover, the implementation of policies under ‘Several Measures to Accelerate the Transformation and Upgrading of Marine Fisheries and to Promote the High-quality Development of Modern Marine Pastures’ positively influences the resilience of fishermen’s livelihoods, though variations in impact are observed among different scenarios. This study not only extends the application of the theoretical framework of livelihood resilience but also dynamically simulates the interactions among various elements influencing the livelihood resilience of fishermen in Guangdong Province.

Using effective records on Chinese marine intangible cultural heritage from CNKI, Wanfang and VIP for 2003–2022, this study uses CiteSpace to analyse and visualise authors, institutions, keywords and their evolution. The findings are threefold. First, publication volume rose sharply in 2017 following the emphasis on strengthening China’s maritime strategy at the 19th National Congress; although research output increased over the two-decade period, its overall scale remained limited. Second, research hotspots mainly concern the development of individual marine-heritage cases and approaches to heritage preservation and transmission. Third, emerging research frontiers include supporting rural revitalisation through marine intangible cultural heritage and promoting sustainable development through living transmission, digital technologies and other innovative approaches. Future research can be broadened and deepened through interdisciplinary work, learning from international experience, stronger collaboration and exchange, and focused case studies.

The symbiotic relationship between enhancing fishermen’s livelihood resilience and the sustainable development of fisheries is increasingly significant. In recent times, the frequent occurrence of climate-related and natural disasters poses substantial risks to the livelihoods of fishermen in Guangdong Province. This context underscores the urgency of analysing factors that influence the resilience of fishermen’s livelihoods, which is crucial for disaster resistance and resilience enhancement. Utilising a three-dimensional livelihood resilience framework, this paper explores the endogenous relationships and resilience trends among various factors within the livelihood resilience system of fishermen in Guangdong Province. Additionally, it forecasts and simulates the resilience shifts of exogenous variables across multiple scenarios under the policy of ‘Remote Utilization and Ecological Development’. Our findings indicate that the key components bolstering the livelihood resilience of Guangdong’s fishermen include their capacity for learning, buffering, and self-organisation. Each system incorporates a ‘disaster prevention – disaster reduction – disaster relief’ cycle to combat disastrous impacts effectively. Moreover, the implementation of policies under ‘Several Measures to Accelerate the Transformation and Upgrading of Marine Fisheries and to Promote the High-quality Development of Modern Marine Pastures’ positively influences the resilience of fishermen’s livelihoods, though variations in impact are observed among different scenarios. This study not only extends the application of the theoretical framework of livelihood resilience but also dynamically simulates the interactions among various elements influencing the livelihood resilience of fishermen in Guangdong Province.
